decisionsTitle: «Punctele planului»: the volunteers' points typed by hand on «Planul voluntarilor» — on the route or at the start–finish — with their coordinates and a link to the map (amending §949, §953 and §956)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-17, on a phone, four days before Saturday's race and the day after «Planul voluntarilor» got its picture and its email:** «După ce încarc acea poză cu harta de voluntari vreau să pot defini punctele de mână, să pun nume punct și la ce km e și coordonate punct». And minutes later: «Practic voluntarii sunt de 2 tipuri: start-finish și pe traseu».

**What was there.** The plan's picture is the organizers' map with the volunteers' points numbered on it. The plan's points were only the event's public «Puncte pe traseu» (§757), kept in the event's editor — every one of them on the event's page, the route's chart and the race number — and whoever works at the start and the finish (the desk, the kits, the start line, the finish line) stood under «Fără punct pe traseu», among the people nobody had placed yet.

**Decision.** The plan has points of its own, typed on the plan's page, and knows its two kinds of volunteers by where they stand. A point of the plan is **on the route** — a name, the kilometre it is at, a number in the route's order — or **at the start–finish** — a name; no kilometre said anywhere, no number. Any point, the editor's too, may also say where it is: its coordinates, which the plan's page and the volunteer's own email turn into a link to a map.

**The two kinds are kinds of point, not of person.** A volunteer already stands at one point (`event_volunteers.checkpoint_id`, §949). With the kind on the point, a person's kind is where they stand: nothing second is stored about the person, so nothing has to be kept in step when somebody is moved from the kits to a junction.

**The plan's own points stay off every public page.** The owner asked to define the volunteers' points, not to publish them — and in the race's own week, when a point typed on a phone must not appear on the event's page, on the route's chart or on a race number already at the printer's. So a point added on the plan is the plan's alone (`plan_only`).

**The data** (migration `0211`, expand only). Four columns on `event_checkpoints` — `plan_only` and `start_finish` (booleans, false for every row from before), `latitude numeric(8,6)` and `longitude numeric(9,6)` (nullable) — and three CHECKs: a start–finish point is a plan-only one; the coordinates are both there or both absent; each is within ±90 and ±180. One table, because the reference a volunteer's row holds is to this table: a second table would need a second reference and a rule that only one of the two is set. A plan-only point keeps the table's own rules: the one name the organizers typed stands in both name columns — it is their own word for a place («Kituri», «Intersecția de la izvor»), published nowhere, so there is nothing to translate —, it has no kinds, no time limit and no note, and is never on the chart; a start–finish point's kilometre column holds 0 and nobody reads it.

**Nothing public changes — by construction, not by remembering.** `event-checkpoints/checkpoints.ts` is what every public reader goes through. Its one read of «the event's list», `listCheckpoints`, now leaves the plan-only rows out, and its `Checkpoint` type has no field for the kind or the coordinates. So the event's page (its table and its chart), the preview, the race number, the editor's card, the event's file — export and import —, «Duplică» and a series' dates are what they were; the editor's save, an import and a copy never touch, delete, renumber or carry a plan-only point; an update of a kept row sets only the columns it always set, so a point's coordinates stay through a save and through an import; the editor's limit of thirty counts the editor's points only; and a point of the plan standing past the route's length breaks no event save. The race number's stamp in SQL (`events/repository.ts`) leaves the same rows out, so a point of the plan added, moved or deleted is no new picture address. Every update and delete of that file also carries the filter, so no id, however it arrived, lets the editor's side write to a point of the plan.

**One reader, one order, one number.** The volunteers' side has its own reader, `volunteers/plan-points.ts#listPlanPoints`: every point of the event in the plan's one order — the start–finish points first, in the order they were added, with no number; then the route by kilometre, at one kilometre the editor's points first (in their own order) and then the plan's own in the order they were added, numbered from 1. The editor's points and the plan's own share the one count: it is the route's order, which is what the numbers on the organizers' picture follow. «The order they were added» is a counter kept on the row under the event's lock, never the clock. The plan's page, the «Voluntari» list's «Punct» column and the email all read that list (`readVolunteerPlan`, `point-mail.ts`), so a point is «3» everywhere or nowhere. The reader lives in `modules/volunteers/`, not beside `listCheckpoints`: nothing under `event-checkpoints/`, which the public pages import, can then hand a plan-only point or a coordinate to them, and one list holds who may import it.

**The verbs** (`changePlanPoint`, the same file), for whoever works the volunteers (`canManageVolunteers`: the Organizer and the Administrators), asked by each Server Action at its own door and again by the service before anything is read; the Tehnic role, the Redactor, a desk Volunteer and a member are refused with nothing written.

- **«Adaugă punctul»** — where the point is («Pe traseu», chosen as drawn, or «La start–finish»), its name (trimmed, its inner spaces folded, 1 to 60 characters), the kilometre of a route point (required; a comma or a point, two decimals, 0 to 9999.99 — read as the editor reads one, but held to no route's length: the plan is the organizers' own, and no file is read for it) and its coordinates (optional). At the start–finish the kilometre is not read, whatever was posted. At most forty of the plan's own points an event, both kinds together, counted under the event row's lock.
- **«Salvează punctul»** — of a point added here, all of it, the kind included: moved to the start–finish it loses its kilometre, moved to the route it needs one. Of an editor's point, **only the coordinates**: its name and kilometre are public and are changed in the editor, so whatever else such a form posts is never read.
- **«Șterge punctul»** — a point added here only; an editor's point is deleted in the editor. It asks first, with the point's name and how many people stand there. They stand at no point again (the reference's own `ON DELETE SET NULL`) and stay on the plan.

A press that changes nothing writes nothing. Each change is one audit row — `volunteer_plan.point_added`, `point_changed`, `point_removed` — with the point's id, whether it is the plan's own, and its place, name, kilometre and coordinates before and after; a removal also says how many people it freed (those on the plan: a cancelled person is on none). A count, never a person. Nothing here emails anybody, moves a person's state or number, or expires a public cache tag: no public page reads these rows.

**The coordinates** (`event-checkpoints/domain/coordinates.ts`, pure). What a person pastes from a maps application is read into a latitude and a longitude of six decimals: «45.64271, 25.58871», the shape Google Maps copies; a space or a semicolon between the two; decimal commas where the two numbers can still be told apart («45,64271; 25,58871»); a degree sign and the letters N, S, E, W and the Romanian V; degrees, minutes and seconds as Google Maps shows them on a computer; a `geo:` address; and a maps link that carries the pair in the open — `@lat,lon`, `q=`, `query=`, `ll=`, `destination=`, the place written as the link's own path, and, where a link has it, the pin's own pair rather than the centre the map was looking at. Anything else, a latitude past ±90 and a longitude past ±180 are refused with one sentence: write them as Google Maps does, for example 45.64271, 25.58871. **Nothing is ever fetched**: a shortened share link carries no numbers and would have to be followed, so it is refused with that sentence. The pair is written back one way in both languages, «45.64271, 25.58871» — points as decimal marks, which is what a maps application takes back — and «Deschide pe hartă» is Google Maps' own «open this place» address built from the two numbers: a link only, nothing loaded from it and nothing about a person sent to it (`www.google.com` joins the provider hosts with that reason).

**The page.** «Punctele planului» stands right under the picture the points are drawn on and above «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», never on the paper: a help paragraph and «Adaugă un punct» — «Unde e punctul?», «Nume punct», «La ce km e», «Coordonate (opțional)». It is a kept form: a refusal names its box and costs none of the others, and a press that went through comes back to the section with the form empty, so the organizers add their points one after another. It works with scripts off, where the kilometre's box is simply there and not read for a start–finish point — no island was written to hide it. The plan's list is in two groups, each under its own heading on the page and on the paper: «Start–finish», its points by their names alone, and «Pe traseu», the numbered points. A group with no point says so in one quiet line off the paper; a plan with no point at all says the points can be added right there or in the event's editor. The summary says four numbers: how many people are at the start–finish, on the route and at no point, and how many points have nobody. A point with coordinates says them, with «Deschide pe hartă» (the numbers alone on paper), and a route point of the plan's own wears a quiet «doar pe plan». Each point folds open onto «Modifică punctul» — every box for a point added here, the coordinates alone for an editor's, with the sentence that its name and kilometre are the editor's — and, last, «Șterge punctul». A refused save or delete lands at the page's alert with its sentence, as every press of this page does (§953). Every press of it is a thumb's, 44 pixels at least — the two choices of «Unde e punctul?», «Adaugă punctul», «Deschide pe hartă», the bar of «Modifică punctul», «Salvează punctul» and «Șterge punctul» — and nothing of it is wider than a 320-pixel screen. The group «Fără punct pe traseu» is now «Fără punct»: with a group of their own, the people of the start, the kits and the finish are no longer «not on the route», and what is left is who stands at no point at all; its help says where to put them, and the toast of «Scoate» names the group by its new word.

**The «Voluntari» list.** «Punct» says a route point as before — its number and its name — and a start–finish point by its name and the quiet word «start–finish», never a number or a kilometre. No new column, filter or sort.

**The email** (amending §956). A person at the start–finish is told their place with no number and no kilometre: the band reads «Ești la start–finish: Kituri», and the words under it «Organizatorii te-au pus la start–finish: locul tău e cel scris mai sus»; everything else of the message — the event's day and place, what they do, the contact, the picture — is a route point's. They are counted, told and «already told» exactly as the people on the route are. A point that has coordinates when the message leaves adds «Unde e punctul» under the band: the two numbers and «Deschide pe hartă», in the HTML and in the plain text, each half in its language. For a route point without coordinates not a word of the message changed: the messages built by the release before and by this one were compared — subject, text and HTML, in both languages, with and without the picture — and are identical. A text the club rewrote for this message under «Emailuri» replaces the words alone, for both kinds; the band and «Unde e punctul» are the platform's lines around it. **Who «already knows their point» is not changed by this**: a person told before the coordinates were typed stays told, and «Trimite din nou tuturor» is how the organizers send the place.

**The guards.** `tests/unit/volunteers/plan-points-never-leave.test.ts` holds three lists — the files that may import the plan's reader, by the alias or by a relative path; the files that may name the plan's side of a point; and the files that may read the table at all, each held to how it reads. `tests/integration/events/plan-points-stay-private.test.ts` holds every public reader and writer to what it returned and wrote, with a route point of the plan's own, a start–finish point and a point with coordinates in the table. `plan-never-leaves.test.ts` lists the new module as the plan's.

**Refused.**

- *A second table for the plan's points.* A volunteer's row would need a second reference and a rule that one of the two is empty, and every reader of «who stands where» would read both.
- *A kind on the volunteer («start–finish» / «pe traseu»).* A second thing about a person that must agree, on every move, with the point they stand at.
- *Publishing a point added on the plan.* The owner asked for the volunteers' points; the event's page and the race number are not the place for a marshal's corner, least of all in the race's own week.
- *Following a shortened maps link to read its coordinates.* The server would call an address a person pasted; the numbers are one long press away in the same application.
- *A map drawn on the page.* A dependency and a provider's script, for what a link does.
- *Holding a plan's point to the route's length.* That reads the route's file from the store, for a kilometre the organizers typed to tell their own people.

**Not done.** Making a plan-only point public, or the reverse (a public point is added in the editor, as before). An editor's point at the start–finish. Kinds, a note or a time limit on a plan-only point. The coordinates of an editor's point in the event's file, in a copy, on the event's page or anywhere public. A map drawn on the page. A filter of the «Voluntari» list by the kind of point. Marking people as «to tell again» when a point's place changes. The point's coordinates in the volunteers' Excel and CSV. Moving a point of the plan's own up or down among the others added at the same kilometre.
changelogLine: - **«Punctele planului»: the volunteers' points typed by hand on «Planul voluntarilor»** — a point on the route (its name, its kilometre, a number in the route's order) or at the start–finish (its name alone), each with optional coordinates and «Deschide pe hartă»; the plan lists them in two groups, the «Voluntari» list and «Punctul tău» say a start–finish point with no number and no kilometre, and the email adds where a point is. A point added here is never on the event's page, the route's chart, a race number, the event's file or a copy. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Migration `0211_plan_points` is expand-only: on `event_checkpoints`, `plan_only` and `start_finish` (booleans, not null, default false), `latitude numeric(8,6)` and `longitude numeric(9,6)` (nullable), and the CHECKs `event_checkpoints_start_finish_plan_only` (a start–finish point is a plan-only one), `event_checkpoints_coordinates_pair` (both coordinates or neither) and `event_checkpoints_coordinates_range` (±90, ±180); on a database migrated by the release before, every point reads false, false and no coordinates, and each CHECK refuses what it names (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event, then `listPlanPoints` returns every point of it — the editor's «Puncte pe traseu» and the points added on the plan's page — each with `planOnly`, `startFinish`, its coordinates and its `number`, in one order: the start–finish points first, in the order they were added, with no number; then the points on the route by kilometre, at one kilometre the editor's first in their own order and then the plan's own in the order they were added, numbered from 1. `readVolunteerPlan`, the «Voluntari» list's «Punct» column and `volunteerPointAtSend` read that list, so a point has the same number — or none — on the plan's page, in the list's cell and in the email; a person is placed at a point of the plan's own exactly as at an editor's (`changeVolunteer`, `setCheckpoint`), and «Toate datele unei persoane» names it (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event, then a staff member who works the volunteers may add a point of the plan's own (`changePlanPoint`, `add`): a place that is «Pe traseu» or «La start–finish» (anything else refused), a name trimmed and folded to 1–60 characters, for a route point a kilometre — required, a comma or a point, two decimals, 0 to 9999.99, not held to the route's length — and for a start–finish point none (what was posted is not read and 0 is stored), and optional coordinates; at most 40 such points an event, both kinds together, counted under the event row's lock. `edit` changes all of a plan's own point, its kind included (to the start–finish it loses its kilometre, to the route it needs one), and of an editor's point only the coordinates — a posted name, kilometre or place for it is never read or written. `remove` deletes a plan's own point only (an editor's is refused, `VALIDATION_ERROR`); the people who stood there stand at no point again, and the result says how many. Another event's point and one that is not there are `NOT_FOUND`; a press that changes nothing writes and audits nothing; each change writes one audit row (`volunteer_plan.point_added`, `point_changed`, `point_removed`) with the point's id, kind, name, kilometre and coordinates before and after and, for a removal, a count of the people freed — never a person; and none of it queues an email or expires a public cache tag (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

`parseCoordinates` reads what a person pastes from a maps application into a latitude and a longitude of six decimals: «45.64271, 25.58871», a space or a semicolon between the two, decimal commas where the two numbers can still be told apart, a degree sign and the letters N, S, E, W and V (the Romanian west), degrees-minutes-seconds, a `geo:` address, and a maps link that carries the pair in the open (`@`, `q=`, `query=`, `ll=`, `destination=`); an empty box is «none»; anything else, a latitude beyond ±90, a longitude beyond ±180 and a shortened link with no numbers are refused (`VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the box, with the sentence «…ca în Google Maps, de exemplu 45.64271, 25.58871») and nothing is ever fetched. `formatCoordinates` writes «45.64271, 25.58871» in both languages, and `mapUrlOf` builds Google Maps' «open this place» address from the pair alone (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 229 in how the plan's page lists the points. Given the page `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari`, then a section «Punctele planului» (`#plan-points`) stands under the plan's picture and above «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», never on the printed plan, with the form «Adaugă un punct»: «Unde e punctul?» («Pe traseu», chosen as drawn, or «La start–finish»), «Nume punct», «La ce km e» and «Coordonate (opțional)»; a refused press keeps what was typed and names its box, and one that went through comes back to the section with the form empty; it works with scripts off. The plan's list is in two groups under their headings, on the page and on paper — «Start–finish», its points with no number and no kilometre, and «Pe traseu», the numbered points — a group with no point saying so in one line off the paper, and a plan with no point at all saying the points can be added there or in the event's editor; the summary says how many people are at the start–finish, on the route and at no point, and how many points have nobody. A point with coordinates says them with «Deschide pe hartă» (a new tab; the numbers alone on paper), a route point of the plan's own says «doar pe plan», and each point folds open onto «Modifică punctul» — every box for a plan's own point, the coordinates alone for an editor's, with the sentence that its name and kilometre are changed in the editor — and «Șterge punctul», which asks first with the point's name and how many people stand there. A save comes back to its point (`#point-<id>`), a delete to the list, and a refused one to the page's alert with its sentence (`?planError=CODE#admin-alert`) (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 229 in what the «Voluntari» list's «Punct» column says. Given a volunteer placed at a start–finish point, then the cell says the point's name and the quiet word «start–finish», never a number or a kilometre; a volunteer at a point on the route reads as before, the point's number in the plan's one order and its name; no column, filter or sort is added (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The plan's points are changed only by a role that works the volunteers — the Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator (`canManageVolunteers`) — asserted on the server twice: `addPlanPointAction`, `editPlanPointAction` and `removePlanPointAction` ask the capability at their own door, and `changePlanPoint` asks it again before anything is read; the Tehnic role, the Redactor, a desk Volunteer and a member are refused (`FORBIDDEN`) with nothing written and nothing audited, whatever the page drew (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event whose volunteers' plan has points of its own — on the route or at the start–finish — and points with coordinates, then none of it is public: `listCheckpoints` and every reader behind it — the event page's table «Puncte pe traseu» and its chart, the preview, the race number and its picture's stamp (in SQL too), the editor's card, the event's file and a copy of the event — return exactly what they return without them, a `Checkpoint` having no field for the kind or the coordinates; the editor's save, an import and a copy never touch, delete, renumber or carry a plan-only point, a kept row keeps its coordinates through a save and through an import, the editor's limit of thirty counts the editor's points only, and a plan's point past the route's length refuses no event save. `tests/unit/volunteers/plan-points-never-leave.test.ts` holds the lists of the files that may import the plan's reader, name the plan's side of a point or read the table (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 93 in what a `VOLUNTEER_POINT` says of the point. Given a volunteer at a start–finish point, then the band reads «Ești la start–finish: {name}» / "You are at the start–finish: {name}" and the words under it say the start–finish, with no number and no kilometre anywhere in the HTML or the text; the subject, the event's day and place, the roles, the contact and the picture are as for a point on the route. Given a point that has coordinates when the message leaves, then each half says, under the band, «Unde e punctul» / "Where the point is" with the two numbers and «Deschide pe hartă» / "Open on the map" — a link in the HTML, its address written out in the text. For a point on the route without coordinates the message is word for word what it was (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 68 to 70 in what a point is. Given «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», then a point is any point of the plan's one list — an editor's, one added on the plan's page, or one at the start–finish: the people at each are counted, written to, withdrawn and «already told» alike, and a row naming another event's point stands at none. Who «already knows their point» does not change when a point's name, kilometre, kind or coordinates do: a person told before the coordinates were typed stays told, and «Trimite din nou tuturor» writes to them again; a message rendered after a change says the point as it stands then (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Punctele planului» on the volunteers' plan at 320 pixels, then nothing is wider than the screen and every control a thumb must hit is at least 44 pixels tall: «Adaugă punctul», the two choices of «Unde e punctul?», «Deschide pe hartă», the bar of «Modifică punctul», «Salvează punctul» and «Șterge punctul» (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
